Package neqsim.pvtsimulation.flowassurance

Class NaphthenatePrecipitationModel

java.lang.Object
neqsim.pvtsimulation.flowassurance.NaphthenatePrecipitationModel
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class NaphthenatePrecipitationModel extends Object implements Serializable
Equilibrium model for precipitation of organic acid (naphthenate) salts from crude oil in contact with produced water.

Two acid classes are followed:

  • Monoprotic naphthenic acids (HA), quantified by the total acid number (TAN). They partition between oil and water, dissociate in water and can form a calcium carboxylate soap CaA2. The dissociated acid in the water is also the driver for sodium carboxylate soap emulsions.
  • Tetraprotic ARN acids (H4A), the C80 tetraacids responsible for hard calcium naphthenate deposits. They stay in the oil and react at the oil-water interface with calcium.

Equilibria

 HA(oil)  = HA(water)                   P     = [HA]oil / [HA]water
 HA(water) = H+ + A-                    Ka    = a(H+) a(A-) / [HA]water
 CaA2(s)  = Ca2+ + 2 A-                 Ksp   = a(Ca2+) a(A-)^2
 H4A(oil) + 2 Ca2+ = Ca2A(s) + 4 H+     K_ARN = a(H+)^4 / ([H4A]oil a(Ca2+)^2)
 CO2(g) + H2O = H+ + HCO3-              K1 KH = a(H+) a(HCO3-) / p(CO2)

The monoacid part has the structure of the thermodynamic naphthenate model of Mohammed and Sorbie (2010). Ion activity coefficients are from the Davies equation. The water pH is either given, or calculated from the CO2 partial pressure and the bicarbonate alkalinity of the brine; in the latter case the protons released by acid dissociation and salt formation consume alkalinity, so the pH is solved together with the precipitation. The CO2 route describes the main field mechanism: pressure reduction strips CO2 from the water, the pH rises and the acids dissociate.

Predictive and calibrated use

The default parameters are screening values. The dissociation constant (pKa 4.9) is a measured property of naphthenic acids (Havre et al., 2003). The partition coefficient, the solubility product of the calcium soap and the ARN constant are not universal: they depend on the acid structure distribution of the crude and are set to defaults that reproduce typical field onset behaviour (see the setter documentation). Until parameters are regressed to bottle-test or field data with NaphthenateModelFitting, results are a ranking and sensitivity tool, and isCalibrated() returns false.

References:

  • Mohammed, M.A., Sorbie, K.S. (2010). Thermodynamic modelling of calcium naphthenate formation: model predictions and experimental results. Colloids and Surfaces A, 369, 1-10.
  • Havre, T.E., Sjoblom, J., Vindstad, J.E. (2003). Oil/water-partitioning and interfacial behavior of naphthenic acids. J. Dispersion Sci. Technol., 24(6), 789-801.
  • Sjoblom, J., Simon, S., Xu, Z. (2014). The chemistry of tetrameric acids in petroleum. Adv. Colloid Interface Sci., 205, 319-338.
  • Turner, M.S., Smith, P.C. (2005). Controls on soap scale formation, including naphthenate soaps - drivers and mitigation. SPE 94339.
  • Plummer, L.N., Busenberg, E. (1982). The solubilities of calcite, aragonite and vaterite in CO2-H2O solutions. Geochim. Cosmochim. Acta, 46, 1011-1040.

    • estimateLogPartitionCoefficient

      public static double estimateLogPartitionCoefficient(double molarMass)
      Estimates the oil/water partition coefficient of an undissociated monoprotic naphthenic acid from its molar mass.

      log10 P = 4.0 + 0.010 (M - 300). This is an engineering default, not a published correlation: it places the pH of half extraction of a 300 g/mol acid into an equal volume of water at about pH 9, in line with the general observation that C15-C20 naphthenic acids transfer to water only at alkaline pH, and makes heavier acids more oil soluble. Replace it by a regressed value when partition data exist.

      Parameters:
      molarMass - acid molar mass (g/mol)
      Returns:
      base-10 logarithm of the oil/water partition coefficient
